data.Description: The 25-year-old will spend the rest of his life in prison following his conviction in the killing of Bethany Ann Israel.
data.Story:
A Lakeville man will spend the rest of his life in prison for the horrific killing of his pregnant sister in 2024.

Jack Joseph Ball, 25, was sentenced on Thursday to two life sentences without the possibility of parole in the death of Bethany Ann Israel and her unborn child.

Prosecutors requested, and Judge Bryce Ehrman agreed, that the life sentences should be served consecutively after Ball was convicted of two counts of premeditated murder.

Israel, 30, was 17-18 weeks pregnant when she was killed and dismembered at Ball’s home on May 23, 2024.

Investigators discovered several journals and other handwritten paperwork belonging to Ball, in which he allegedly described anger over his sister’s pregnancy and said she was “no longer innocent.”

Israel was described as a “cherished wife, daughter, sister and an expectant mother but also a beloved figure in the volleyball community.”

“The defendant’s actions were profoundly disturbing and incomprehensible in their cruelty. His conduct has devastated countless lives and inflicted trauma on our communities,” said Dakota County Attorney Kathy Keena.

“I extend my sincere gratitude to all those who contributed to the investigation and prosecution of his horrific case. I also offer my deepest condolences to Bethany’s family, friends and all those who cherished her.”
